newsitem.title: USA: G7 broadly satisfied with forex mart-Canada source.
newsitem.headline: G7 broadly satisfied with forex mart-Canada source.

text.p: The Group of Seven industrial nations are generally satisfied with the state of currency markets, a senior Canadian Finance Ministry official said on Saturday.

"There have been no major concerns expressed," the official, who declined to be named, told reporters. "People are generally satisfied with the orderly nature of exchange rate movements that have taken place over the recent period."
He said he expects G7 finance ministers and central bankers to touch on the currency issue at their meeting on Saturday, but that it would not be a mjor focus.

The Canadian official said he expects the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- to confirm at their meeting that Paris Club creditor nations are prepared to offer poor nations 80 percent debt relief.
"It looks as though we should be able to secure that today," he said.

The Paris Club currently has a ceiling of 67 percent on the debt relief it provides poor nations. The increased contribution will be part of a three-pronged effort -- by the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and the Paris Club -- to help put debt-ridden poor nations back on their feet.

The Canadian official said the IMF will need to sell some of its gold to finance its contribution to the initiative and the continuation of its Enhanced Structural Adjustment (lending) Facility (ESAF) for poor nations.
"At some point, gold sales will be necessary," he said.

But the precise timing of the sales remains open and will partly depend on the level of bilateral contributions member nations make to ESAF. "It could be (19)98, it could be '99, it could be 2000," he said. "That just is unclear at this point."
The Canadian official said Canada would be open to making a bilateral contribution to the continuation of ESAF.
That would effectively mean allowing the IMF to use the investment income from some $15-1/2 million Canada already has on deposit at the Fund to help finance its stepped-up aid for poor nations.
"We've indicated we're prepared to see how those resources ...could be used to support this initiative," the Canadian official said.
